generation.explanation: The tangent function **y = tan(x) = sin(x)/cos(x)** has vertical asymptotes wherever the denominator **cos(x) = 0**. That happens at **x = π/2 + kπ** for every integer k — so in the window [−2π, 2π], asymptotes appear at **x = ±π/2 and x = ±3π/2**. As x approaches one of these values from the left, tan(x) → +∞; from the right, tan(x) → −∞. The graph never touches these lines — it blows up to infinity instead. Because tan has period π, each branch between consecutive asymptotes is an exact copy of the others. The animation below draws the four branches, marks the asymptotes as dashed lines, and gives you a slider to sweep a point along the curve so you can watch its y-value explode near the asymptotes.
